result.topic_en: Verification by successive reduction of residues that 6^50 leaves remainder 1 on division by 101 and 6^33 leaves remainder 1 on division by 67, followed by a table showing, for bases a = 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 11 and primes 2p+1 in given residue classes, whether a^p-1 or a^p+1 is divisible by 2p+1.

methods.what: Checking whether a^m ≡ 1 (mod q) by working backwards from residue 1, repeatedly adding multiples of q to make the residue divisible by the base, and dividing by the base to lower the exponent

methods.quote: Examinemus potestatem $6^{50}$ num per 101 divisa relinquat $+1$
Examinetur potestas $6^{33}$ an per 67 divisa relinquat $+1$

methods.what: Table, equivalent to Euler's criterion / quadratic character of a, giving for prime 2p+1 in residue classes mod 4a whether 2p+1 divides a^p-1 or a^p+1
methods.quote: Utra formula $a^p\pm1$ per numerum primum $2p+1$ sit divisibilis sequens tabella ostendit:

items.quote: quod quia est verum, patet regula.
items.english: Since this is true, the rule is evident.
